newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT-Ackerstein Ind a buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Ackerstein Ind a buy.

text.p: Israel's Ackerstein Industries was rated a buy in a report released on Wednesday by Bank Hapoalim.

The bank's securities research department said the building-product company's shares were trading on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange at a 30 percent discount. It estimated Ackerstein's underlying value at between $56 million and $62 million as opposed to its market value of around $43 million.

"The firm is coping with competition and a slowdown in the building sector by making wide-scale investments in developing specialty products...and improving technology at its plants in order to save on production costs and wages," the report said.
Bank Hapoalim noted Ackerstein's net profit rose 24.4 percent to 8.5 million shekels in the third quarter of 1996 compared with the same period a year earlier.
The report forecast 1996 net profit at 13.4 million shekels, against 11.1 million shekels in 1995 and said it would rise to 18.2 million shekels this year and to 21 million shekels in 1998.

Ackerstein, established in 1989 from earlier companies, is the sole producer in Israel of silicate blocks, bricks and brick facing. It also makes concrete roof tiles, paving stones and concrete piping lines.
